proposals.before: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose, poured into Pingyang, crowned Cao Hong shanyu, and pillaged widely.
proposals.after: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose against Yao Hong, entered Pingyang, attacked Yao Chengdu of Liyi at the Xiongnu fort, raised the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic rendering omits the attack on 立義姚成都 at 匈奴堡 and the Xiongnu identity of 曹弘.

proposals.before: Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked and set up Yao Chengdu of Liyi at the Xiongnu fort, pushed Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
proposals.after: Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, pushed the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
proposals.reason: 攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡 is an attack on Yao Chengdu, not installing him; 立義 is his title.

proposals.before: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.
proposals.after: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Cao Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Cao Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.
proposals.reason: 討弘 and 執弘 refer to 曹弘, not Yao Hong; bare Hong in English confuses the two men.

proposals.before: Yao Zan retreated to Chouqi.
proposals.after: Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, then withdrew to Chouqi.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 贊至秦州 and reports only the withdrawal to Chouqi.

proposals.before: Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; local leaders blocked him and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao blocked him, and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English replaces the named 胡儼、華韜 with generic 'local leaders'.

proposals.before: Jianjie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.
proposals.after: Lijie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.
proposals.reason: 立節 is Lijie, not Jianjie (建節); the literal rendering copies the wrong title from the earlier Wang Zong passage.

proposals.before: At Hengshui Bobo pulled back to Anding; Hu Yan shut the gates, killed thousands of Xianbei, and handed the city over.
proposals.after: At Hengshui, Bobo pulled back to Anding; Hu Yan shut the gates, killed thousands of Xianbei, and handed the city over.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the place Hengshui with the person Bobo.

proposals.before: Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Cangcang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.
proposals.after: Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Chencang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.
proposals.reason: 陳倉 is Chencang, not Cangcang.

proposals.before: Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Cangcang; Juan fled to Sanguan.
proposals.after: Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Chencang; Juan fled to Sanguan.
proposals.reason: 陳倉 is Chencang, not Cangcang.

proposals.before: Now he is stranded abroad without voice at court; Anding feels doomed—nine tenths want to flee south. Give him forty thousand veterans and he could drum straight on Chang'an—think of the risk!
proposals.after: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, and inside he does not share court power; the men of Anding think themselves isolated and pressed by the raider—nine houses in ten wish to move south. If he rallies forty thousand crack troops and drums his march on the capital, would that not burden the altars?
proposals.reason: The Chinese 若擁精兵四萬 is a warning that Yao Hui might himself rally troops against the capital, not a proposal that the court give him forty thousand men.

proposals.before: Yao Yu plotted with Tan Daoji's party; jealous officers smeared Zhao Xuan and pushed Yao Guang to march out.
proposals.after: Yao Guang's Major Yao Yu was in secret communication with Tan Daoji; Chief Clerk Yan Hui, Yang Qian, and others were all Yu's faction, jealous of Zhao Xuan's loyalty; they slandered him together and firmly urged Guang to go out to battle.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence drops the named officers 閻恢 and 楊虔 and fuses them into unnamed jealous officers.

proposals.before: Soon Liu Yu of Jin massed at Pengcheng and sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e through Huai-Fei against Qiqiu and Xiangcheng while Shen Linzi struck Cangyuan from Bian.
proposals.after: Soon Jin Grand Commandant Liu Yu massed a great host to campaign against Hong, halted at Pengcheng, and sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon-Soaring General Wang Zhen'e in from the Huai and Fei against Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, while General Shen Linzi entered the He from the Bian and struck Cangyuan.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence omits the campaign's named target 泓 and the offices 太尉, 冠軍將軍, 龍驤將軍, and 將軍 that the Chinese and literal supply.

proposals.before: Jin is inside the passes, four provinces are gone, Bobo tears the west—this is the hour to rally for the throne, not to hoard grain.
proposals.after: The Wu invaders are now inside, four provinces have fallen, western raiders disturb the border, and Qin and Liang have been overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is the hour for the lords to rally to the throne.
proposals.reason: 吳寇 is the Wu/Jin invaders, not 'Jin is inside the passes'; 西虜 is unnamed western raiders, not Helian Bobo; 秦、涼覆敗 and 累卵 are omitted.

proposals.before: Yao Yi is dead yet Yao Hui marches on the capital—what now?"
proposals.after: Yi first plotted rebellion and was crushed; Hui again leads hosts in inner revolt—what is to be done?"
proposals.reason: 滅亡 here follows Yi's capture and imprisonment (執懿囚之), not a stated death; idiomatic 'is dead' overstates the Chinese.

proposals.before: Mao Dezu broke Yin Ya at Li, captured him, killed Jin guards, and fled to Tong Pass.
proposals.after: Mao Dezu attacked Hongnong Grand Administrator Yin Ya at Li city; the host broke and Dezu's cavalry seized him; afterward Yin Ya killed the Jin guards and fled to hold Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: 既而殺晉守者奔固潼關 continues Yin Ya as subject after capture, not Mao Dezu; the idiomatic English assigns the killing and flight to the wrong man.

proposals.before: Tong Pass is the bottleneck; if Yao Shao locks it, Wang Zhen'e is lost.
proposals.after: Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of advantageous terrain; Zhen'e is an isolated army, his situation perilous and his force small—if Yao Shao is allowed to hold it, he will be hard to deal with.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents that Wang Zhen'e is already lost and drops the isolated-army, peril, and small-force clauses that the Chinese states.

proposals.before: Tan Daoji counterattacked but broke and withdrew to Dingcheng.
proposals.after: Tan Daoji led Wang Chong, Shen Linzi, and others in a straight charge at Shao's army; the officers and soldiers were startled and scattered and drew back to Dingcheng.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Wang Jing (王敬) and Shen Linzi in the charge; 將士驚散，引還定城 describes Shao's host breaking and withdrawing, not Daoji's defeat.

proposals.before: Yao Luan sent general Yin Ya with Daoji's major Xu Yan south of Tong Pass; he was seized by Yan and sent to Liu Yu.
proposals.after: Yao Luan sent general Yin Ya against Daoji's major Xu Yan south of Tong Pass; Ya was seized by Yan and sent to Liu Yu.
proposals.reason: 與 here is engagement against Xu Yan, not accompaniment; the following 為琰所獲 confirms Yin Ya was the one captured.

proposals.before: Closing quotation: Shao then desisted.
proposals.after: Shao then desisted.
proposals.reason: Literal English inserts a meta note 'Closing quotation' that is not in the Chinese 紹乃止.

proposals.before: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, straight general Duke of Pingyi Yizhan Juan, and raiding general Wang Luosheng to camp in Hedong as sounding support for Hong.
proposals.after: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, Straight General Duke of Anping Yizhan Juan, and Raiding General Wang Luosheng; they advanced to occupy Henei, and Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong, as sounding support for Hong.
proposals.reason: 安平公 is Duke of Anping, not Pingyi; the Chinese also stations the first pair at Henei and Wang Luosheng at Hedong.

proposals.before: Wei sent Baba Song and others to threaten Liu Yu's flank.
proposals.after: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, Straight General Duke of Anping Yizhan Juan, and Raiding General Wang Luosheng to occupy Henei and Hedong as support for Yao Hong.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents a threat to Liu Yu's flank and drops the named Wei officers and posts.

proposals.before: Liu Yu sent Shen Linzi overland to Qingni against Yaoliu.
proposals.after: Liu Yu halted at Shan city and sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand crack troops over the mountains to join Shen Tianzi and others at Qingni, intending to attack Yaoliu.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the halt at Shan, the troop figure, and the junction with Shen Tianzi that the Chinese names.

proposals.before: Liu Yu sent Zhu Chaoshi to strike Puban from the north bank.
proposals.after: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yi to join Xue Bo north of the He to attack Puban.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits Tong Pass, Xu Yi, and Xue Bo, who are named in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Wang Zhen'e crossed the Wei against Yao Nan.
proposals.after: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits Wang Jing (王敬) and treats Liu Yu's dispatch as Wang Zhen'e's solo action.

proposals.before: Yao Zan tried to bring Wei in against Liu Yu's rear.
proposals.after: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Sima Guofan from Zhiguan toward Henei, drawing Wei troops to fall on Liu Yu's rear.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the two Sima commanders and the Zhiguan–Henei route.

proposals.before: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Simo Guofan from Zhiguan toward Hedong, drawing Wei troops to tread on Yu's rear.
proposals.after: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Sima Guofan from Zhiguan toward Henei, drawing Wei troops to tread on Yu's rear.
proposals.reason: Literal English misspells Sima Guofan as Simo and renders 河內 as Hedong.

proposals.before: Yao Hong's generals died to a man; he galloped alone back into the palace.
proposals.after: Yao Chen and forward-army Yao Lie, left guard Yao Bao'an, supernumerary Wang Bo, Jianwei Yao Jin, General Who Displays Might Yao Hao, right aide Sun Xuan and others all died in formation; Hong alone on horseback returned to the palace.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English erases the seven named dead, which the Chinese lists.

proposals.before: Grass and trees withered for a hundred li around Jiankang—omen of the tyrant's fall.
proposals.after: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.
proposals.reason: The omen-of-the-tyrant clause is not in the Chinese and invents interpretation.

proposals.before: Yao Chang used Yao Xiang's legacy to seize Chang'an when Fu Jian fell.
proposals.after: Jingmao took up Zhongxiang's thread, stepped into Fu's fall, whistled command to the heroes, and enlarged the hegemon's enterprise.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents Chang'an and collapses courtesy names and the Han-Qin settlement that continues in the next sentence.

proposals.before: He gave the west to Tufa Lianggu and the north to Helian Bobo, ignored advice, and border disaster followed year on year.
proposals.after: He entrusted the Liang capital to Tufa and handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, and rejecting remonstrance invited calamity.
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 禿髮 and 赫連; 'Lianggu' is not in the source, and the sentence omits inner-wall and yearly-war clauses.

proposals.before: Eulogy: Yao Yizhong died unbroken.
proposals.after: Eulogy: Yao Yizhong was stern and fierce, and in the end displayed remarkable integrity.
proposals.reason: Chinese 剛烈…終表奇節 describes character and integrity, not an explicit death; “died unbroken” invents a death scene.

proposals.before: Yao Xiang was bold; Yao Chang was the cunning founder.
proposals.after: Yao Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Yao Chang was a treacherous champion.
proposals.reason: 實英果 is heroic-resolute, not merely bold; 奸傑 is treacherous champion, and “founder” is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Yao Xing built the state; Yao Hong watched it fall.
proposals.after: Yao Xing first raised the frame; Yao Hong was then destroyed and extinguished.
proposals.reason: 泓遂摧滅 makes Hong the one destroyed, not a spectator watching the state fall.

decisions.after: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose against Yao Hong, entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, raised the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
decisions.reason: The original omits 叛泓, the attack on 立義姚成都 at 匈奴堡, and 匈奴曹弘’s identity as great shanyu. The proposal restores those facts, but “Yao Chengdu of Liyi” reads 立義 as a place; it is his title, so the restored sentence should say Liyi Yao Chengdu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡，推匈奴曹弘為大單于

decisions.reason: 攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡 is an attack on titled Liyi Yao Chengdu, not “attacked and set up”; the replacement matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡

decisions.reason: After 推匈奴曹弘為大單于, 討弘 and 執弘 are Cao Hong (弘), not Yao Hong (泓); spelling out Cao Hong removes a real ambiguity.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 征東姚懿自蒲阪討弘……執弘

decisions.reason: 贊至秦州，退還仇池 records both reaching Qinzhou and withdrawing to Chouqi; the original keeps only the withdrawal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 贊至秦州，退還仇池

decisions.reason: 安定人胡儼、華韜等 are named blockers, not generic local leaders; the replacement restores both names.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安定人胡儼、華韜等率眾距恢

decisions.reason: 立節 is Lijie; Jianjie is 建節 from the Wang Zong sentence and is the wrong title here.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 立節彌姐成

decisions.reason: A comma after Hengshui is only punctuation. “At Hengshui Bobo pulled back to Anding” already reads as an introductory place plus Bobo’s withdrawal; the proposed after does not change meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 軍次橫水，勃勃退保安定

decisions.reason: 陳倉 is Chencang; Cangcang is a wrong transcription of the same place-name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 討楊倦于陳倉

decisions.reason: The same 陳倉 error appears in the literal field; Chencang is the correct reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 討楊倦于陳倉

decisions.reason: 若擁精兵四萬 is a hypothetical that Hui himself might rally forty thousand and drum on the capital, not a suggestion that the court give him the troops. The original also drops 死地, 不豫朝權, and 社稷之累.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若擁精兵四萬，鼓行而向京師，得不為社稷之累乎

decisions.reason: 主簿閻恢、楊虔等 are named members of Yao Yu’s faction; collapsing them into unnamed jealous officers omits persons the Chinese names.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 主簿閻恢、楊虔等皆禹之党

decisions.reason: The original already names Liu Yu of Jin, the halt at Pengcheng, the three generals, and the Huai-Fei and Bian-He routes against Qiqiu, Xiangcheng, and Cangyuan. Dropping 太尉 and the other offices, and leaving 伐泓 implicit in a Yao Hong chapter, is idiomatic condensation, not a mistranslation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓，次於彭城

decisions.reason: 吳寇內侵 is Wu/Jin invaders striking inward, not “Jin is inside the passes”; 西虜 is unnamed western raiders, not Bobo; 秦、涼覆敗 and 累卵 are in this sentence; “not to hoard grain” belongs to the next sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 今吳寇內侵，四州傾沒，西虜擾邊，秦、涼覆敗，朝廷之危有同累卵

decisions.reason: 懿始構逆滅亡 is that Yi’s rebellion was crushed, not a statement that he is dead; the replacement keeps Hui’s inner revolt and drops the invented death.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 懿始構逆滅亡，恢復擁眾內叛

decisions.reason: After 德祖使騎追獲之, 既而殺晉守者奔固潼關 continues Yin Ya as subject; the original wrongly makes Mao Dezu kill the guards and flee.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 德祖使騎追獲之，既而殺晉守者奔固潼關

decisions.reason: 鎮惡孤軍，勢危力寡，若使姚紹據之，則難圖矣 is a warning that Zhen'e is isolated and Shao holding the pass would be hard to handle, not that Zhen'e is already lost.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鎮惡孤軍，勢危力寡，若使姚紹據之，則難圖矣

decisions.after: Tan Daoji led Wang Jing, Shen Linzi, and others in a straight charge at Shao's army; Shao's officers and soldiers were startled and scattered and drew back to Dingcheng.
decisions.reason: 道濟率王敬、沈林子等逆沖紹軍 is a successful charge; 將士驚散，引還定城, followed by 紹留姚鸞, is Shao’s host withdrawing. The original reverses the defeat. The proposal still names 王敬 as Wang Chong and leaves “the officers and soldiers” unattributed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 道濟率王敬、沈林子等逆沖紹軍，將士驚散，引還定城

decisions.reason: 遣將尹雅與道濟司馬徐琰于潼關南 plus 為琰所獲 means Ya was sent against Xu Yan and captured by him, not sent along with him.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 姚鸞遣將尹雅與道濟司馬徐琰于潼關南，為琰所獲

decisions.reason: 紹乃止 has no meta “Closing quotation”; that label is not in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 紹乃止

decisions.reason: 安平公 is Duke of Anping, not Pingyi; 進據河內 applies to Baba Song and Yizhan Juan, while 王洛生屯於河東 is a separate posting.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 正直將軍、安平公乙旃眷，進據河內，遊擊將軍王洛生屯於河東

decisions.reason: 為泓聲援 is sounding support for Hong, not a threat to Liu Yu’s flank; the Chinese names the three Wei officers and the Henei/Hedong posts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 進據河內，遊擊將軍王洛生屯於河東，為泓聲援

decisions.reason: 劉裕次於陝城，遣沈林子率精兵萬餘……會沈田子等於青泥 names the halt at Shan, the troop figure, and the junction with Shen Tianzi, all missing from the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 劉裕次於陝城，遣沈林子率精兵萬餘……會沈田子等於青泥

decisions.reason: 劉裕至潼關，遣將軍硃超石、徐猗之會薛帛于河北 names Tong Pass, Xu Yi, and Xue Bo, which the original drops.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 劉裕至潼關，遣將軍硃超石、徐猗之會薛帛于河北

decisions.reason: 裕遣王鎮惡、王敬 is Liu Yu sending both men from Qiushe; the original makes Wang Zhen'e act alone and omits 王敬.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 裕遣王鎮惡、王敬自秋社西渡渭

decisions.reason: 姚贊遣司馬休之及司馬國璠自軹關向河內 names both Simas and the Zhiguan–Henei route, omitted in the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣司馬休之及司馬國璠自軹關向河內

decisions.reason: 司馬國璠 is Sima Guofan, not Simo; 河內 is Henei, not Hedong (河東).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 司馬休之及司馬國璠自軹關向河內

decisions.after: Yao Chen; Yao Lie of the Vanguard; Yao Bao'an of the Left Guard; Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo; General Who Establishes Martial Might Yao Jin; General Who Displays Might Yao Hao; Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Sun Xuan; and the others all died in battle. Yao Hong rode back to the palace alone.
decisions.reason: The Chinese lists seven named dead and their offices. The revision restores them, renders 建武 as General Who Establishes Martial Might rather than the erroneous 'Jianwei,' and names Yao Hong in the final clause.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 姚諶及前軍姚烈、左衛姚寶安、散騎王帛、建武姚進、揚威姚蠔、尚書右丞孫玄等皆死於陣

decisions.reason: 建康百里之內，草木皆燋死焉 reports scorched vegetation only; “omen of the tyrant’s fall” is invented commentary.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建康百里之內，草木皆燋死焉

decisions.after: Yao Chang took up Yao Xiang's legacy, stepped into Fu Jian's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise, and borrowed Murong Chong's edge to settle Hangu and Qin.
decisions.reason: The original invents seizing Chang'an. This unit still contains 假容沖之銳，俯定函、秦; the proposal wrongly treats that clause as the next sentence and replaces readable names with unexplained courtesy names. Keep the identifications and restore Hangu and Qin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 景茂因仲襄之緒，躡苻亡之會，嘯命群豪，恢弘霸業，假容沖之銳，俯定函、秦

decisions.after: He entrusted the Liang capital to Tufa and handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity, inner-wall strife broke out again and again, war had no quiet year, and men lived in fear.
decisions.reason: 禿髮 has no given name Lianggu, and 涼都/朔方 are not simply west/north. The proposal still drops 蕭牆屢發，戰無寧歲，人有危心, which belong to this sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 委涼都於禿髮，授朔方於赫連，專己生災，邊城繼陷，距諫招禍，蕭牆屢發，戰無寧歲，人有危心

decisions.reason: 剛烈……終表奇節 is a character judgment of sternness and remarkable integrity, not a death scene.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 弋仲剛烈，終表奇節

decisions.reason: 襄實英果 is truly heroic and resolute, not merely bold; 萇惟奸傑 is a treacherous champion, not a “cunning founder.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 襄實英果，萇惟奸傑

decisions.reason: 泓遂摧滅 makes Hong the one destroyed and extinguished, not a spectator who watched the state fall.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 興始崇構，泓遂摧滅

claimRetractions.reason: 為琰所獲 makes Yin Ya the captive of Xu Yan. The claim that Yin Ya captured Xu Yan exists only if 與 is read as accompaniment and the capture is inverted; the Chinese supports no such fact.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 為琰所獲，送之劉裕

sourceDate.text: 劉裕伐後秦、潼關蒲阪之役

claimRevisions.reason: 王敬 is Wang Jing; the English personal name Wang Chong is a bad transcription of 敬, not a source form.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 道濟率王敬、沈林子等逆沖紹軍

claimRevisions.reason: This unit names only 禿髮. The given name Lianggu is not in the Chinese and must be removed from the personal-name claim.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 委涼都於禿髮
